Clarity.justification: The paper is exceptionally well-written with a logical structure (Introduction, Related Work, Methodology, Experiments, Results, Discussion). Ideas such as representational alignment, structured error formatting (PROBLEM/LOCATION/CONTEXT/ROOT_CAUSE), and the scrambled control condition are clearly articulated. Tables, figures, and sub-hypotheses (H-E1, H-M1–H-M3, H-C1) are presented coherently with explicit success criteria.

Novelty.justification: The work presents original contributions by treating error message format as an independent variable and providing the first causal test via paired structured-vs-scrambled conditions (+14.4 pp, p<0.001). The integration of scaffolding theory with fix-specificity levels (0–3) and the representational-alignment hypothesis are novel angles not explored in prior self-repair literature (Chen et al. 2024, Madaan et al. 2023).

Soundness.justification: Multiple core experiments rely on simulation or mock data rather than real model inference. H-M3 explicitly states results are from synthetic records because of flash_attn CUDA errors; H-M1 uses regex-based mock extraction instead of a real LLM judge; H-M2 and H-C1 results are generated from synthetic BASE_RATES or mock_run_paired_condition functions. Consequently, reported p-values, inverted-U curves, and 100% reconstruction accuracies are not obtained from actual LLM executions, violating the requirement that experimental results be reliable and consistent with the code.

Significance.justification: The problem of improving LLM self-repair via interface design is important, yet the lack of validated real-model results (three of five hypotheses either simulated or non-significant) limits the practical impact. The claimed causal evidence and scaffolding-theory extension cannot be considered reliable without actual inference runs, reducing the likelihood of lasting field impact.

strengths: Clear articulation of a novel causal experimental design (structured vs. scrambled) that isolates format from content.
Well-organized methodology with explicit sub-hypotheses, statistical tests, and reproducibility artifacts (seeded randomization, EvalPlus benchmarks).
weaknesses: Core quantitative claims rest on synthetic/mock data rather than real LLM inference, as evidenced by simulation-mode code paths and flash_attn/CUDA failures.
H-M3, H-M1, and portions of H-M2/H-C1 results are generated from synthetic records or regex mocks, rendering statistical significance and effect sizes non-reproducible on actual models.
